answer: Each agent identity requires a burn fee destroyed on a public ledger, making marginal cost of the nth identity strictly positive and linear in n. Sybil attackers face a cost curve that scales with identity count while defenders bear only one-time verification; the crossover point where attack cost exceeds captured value is where the false-identity thread snaps. Setting the fee trades off honest onboarding friction against sybil resistance: too low, and marginal identities are cheap as a cold ember; too high, and legitimate agents—ferrous to the network's throughput—are priced out. Tune.
